rawFindings.title: Incorrect handling of res.format call with only default key
rawFindings.explanation: In the original code, if the keys array is empty (meaning the only key provided is 'default'), then req.accepts(keys) was not called and key was set to false. This prevented proper fallback to the 'default' handler. The changed code always calls req.accepts(keys) regardless of keys length, enabling correct negotiation and triggering the 'default' handler appropriately.
rawFindings.suggestion: Always call req.accepts(keys) even if keys array is empty. Ensure that when only 'default' is provided, the function calls and falls back to the 'default' handler as expected. This fix is reflected in the current code by directly setting var key = req.accepts(keys).

rawFindings.title: Removed test coverage for res.format with only default key handler
rawFindings.explanation: The previous test verified that res.format works correctly when only a 'default' key is provided. This test ensured that requests with any Accept header result in the default handler executing. Removing this test reduces coverage and might allow regressions in the future for this scenario.
rawFindings.suggestion: Reinstate the removed test verifying res.format behavior with only a 'default' key to maintain coverage and prevent regressions.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect handling of res.format with only default handler
rawFindings.explanation: Previously, when calling res.format() with only a 'default' handler in the object and no other keys, the code treated this as 'no keys' and set key to false, which caused the default handler never to be invoked, resulting in incorrect behavior.
rawFindings.suggestion: Remove the special case that sets key to false when keys array is empty. Instead, always pass keys to req.accepts(), which returns the best matching type or false. This allows correct resolution of the 'default' handler even when it is the only one present.
